I made one small safeguard: the 'ONE ENTITY ONLY' replace keeps its clue-word check, but with the head-noun exception, so it should not hurt answers like Gadsden Purchase. Success-driven edits cover patterns the failure edits do not: proverb completion, answers next to the clue on non-archive pages, series base names, decoy names inside quoted titles, and bridging passages for epithet clues. They are kept as lower-priority additions. I trimmed gold-specific examples from them (answer-bearing examples, site names, specific epithets), as the optimizer memory advises, and gave the Bridge bullet a leading newline so it does not splice into the previous bullet. edits.content: **MANDATORY ANSWER LINE (write it before the answer tags; use it as the check line required in the strategic block below):** `Type: <noun the clue asks for> | Evidence: <quoted passage line, or own fact tied to one distinctive clue detail> | Check: <candidate put into the clue's blank reads correctly and is not a clue word>`. Then give the bare answer.

edits.target: ## Rule 2: Answer the referent, not a word from the clue
edits.content:
- SLOT TEST: put your candidate into the clue's blank. If the result is the wrong kind of thing, or repeats a noun already in the clue, reject it. (Exception: when the clue's own 'this <type>' is the head of the named entity, as in 'this purchase' -> Gadsden Purchase, keep the head.) Three common traps:
  - OWNER / INGREDIENT: when the clue names something that belongs to, is made from, or is located in the answer ('the university of this U.S. territory', 'the capital of this country', 'sauce made from these berries'), answer the owner or ingredient itself, NOT the derived phrase ('University of X', 'Berry sauce'). Strike the clue's own noun and any compound built from it. Keep the plural when the clue says 'these'.
  - CREATOR: 'his/her/its <work>' clues (a quoted title, a foreign-language title, a translation) ask for the CREATOR or OWNER, never the work or its title. If your candidate is the title already quoted in the clue, switch to the person who made it.
  - CONTAINER: 'one of the buildings / wings / rooms / towers at this site (castle, campus, museum, prison)', especially with 'named for <person>', asks for the WHOLE site that contains the part. Reject any candidate containing a name from the clue ('<Person> Tower') and answer with the containing place.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
## Rule 1: Questions are Jeopardy-style clues; always answer with the missing entity
edits.content: - A clue that is only ONE bare place name is a category-style fragment. The answer is the larger entity the passages tie it to: a city or region -> its country (a U.S. city -> its state if no country fits). Never repeat the clue word. Passages saying 'second-largest city in <Country>' -> that country.

edits.target: - If the context offers several candidates (a different player in the same article, a film and its song), pick the one that satisfies ALL distinctive details: exact numbers, team, years, place. Do not choose one that fits only some.
edits.content: - ROLE / TIME QUALIFIERS must fit the candidate: 'former first lady', 'ex-', 'widow of', 'then-governor'. If the most-mentioned name held a different role, reject it. Look for a passage that literally pairs the clue's role phrase with a name and take that person, even if the page's main topic is someone more famous.

edits.target: - Put only the bare answer in the answer tags. Do not write a sentence, restate the clue, or add dates, qualifiers or alternatives. Brief reasoning belongs before the tags.
edits.content: - Put only the bare answer in the answer tags. Do not write a sentence, restate the clue, or add dates or qualifiers. ONE ENTITY ONLY: never write 'X or Y' or 'X and Y'. When passages list several candidates ('sheep or goat intestines'), commit to the first-listed or most repeated one. Before the tags, check that no word of your answer is a content word of the clue (unless the clue's own 'this <type>' is the head of the named entity, per the exception above). Brief reasoning belongs before the tags.

edits.target: - Use the shortest standard form that names the entity, as a trivia answer key would. If the clue says 'this vitamin', answer with just the letter. If the clue names a group or band, give the group's name only. For people, prefer the form used in a verbatim answer from the context (Rule 3); otherwise use the name form most natural for the clue.
edits.content: - Use the shortest standard form that names the entity, as a trivia answer key would. For people, prefer the form used in a verbatim answer from the context (Rule 3); otherwise use the name form most natural for the clue.

edits.target: - NEVER answer 'Not answerable', 'True/False', 'Yes/No', or a description of the clue. Always output the specific entity, word, or name that the clue is asking for.
edits.content: - Proverb, saying or quotation clues ('According to an old proverb, "Its mother is necessity"', 'Spare the rod and...') ask for the missing word of the saying. Recall the full saying and answer with the one word the pronoun or blank stands for, never a word the clue already quotes.

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'. Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - Other page layouts also carry the answer next to the clue. (a) Quiz, flashcard and forum pages print the clue followed directly by the answer in CAPITALS, after a comma, or as a user's guess ('..., is that X?'). Treat that trailing word as the lead candidate, confirm it against the other passages, and answer in normal form. (b) Search-aggregator results ('answers' sites, Quizlet-like pages) may show the clue in the snippet while the [TLE] page title is the answer ('<answer> - Search-ID.com'). Strip the site name. Use the title only when the snippet really repeats the clue's distinctive words; a title that merely shares a topic word is not evidence.

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'This film series / franchise / TV series / book series' asks for the SERIES base name shared by all installments the passages mention, not one sequel number or subtitle they dwell on. A clue that says 'this film' or 'this novel' (one work) wants that single title, keeping a leading 'The' when it is part of the title.

edits.target: - A word in quotation marks inside the clue (a 'drag', a nickname) is usually a pun or hint tied to the answer. Look for passages where that word appears next to a candidate and answer with that candidate.
edits.content: - A work's title in quotation marks inside the clue is an anchor, and a name inside that title is a decoy, not the answer. Find the passage line that ties the title to the entity the clue wants (a subtitle, possessive or byline such as "<Person>'s Favorite Recipes" or 'by <Author>'). Answer with that entity in the form the passages repeat.

edits.target: let the unique detail win (Khartoum -> Sudan even if Sudan is no longer 'largest').
edits.content: - Bridge the clue to one passage: find the sentence that restates the clue's facts with a name in the 'this X' slot and take that name in the short form the passages use. For an epithet or nickname in the clue, quoted or not, prefer the passage that links the epithet and the clue's topic word or anchor to one name, ignore passages where the epithet word appears only in an unrelated title, and answer with the real or official name, not the nickname. 'South of <town> in this state' or 'monarch of this nation' asks for the state or nation containing the anchor, not the town, dynasty or a smaller realm.
